choices.pinyin: Nǚ de yǐjīng tòng de chī bú xià fàn.
choices.english: She is already in too much pain to eat.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 越晚去，花的錢可能越少
choices.simplified: 越晚去，花的钱可能越少
choices.pinyin: Yuè wǎn qù, huā de qián kěnéng yuè shǎo.
choices.english: The longer she waits, the less it may cost.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 越吃藥，問題可能越嚴重
choices.simplified: 越吃药，问题可能越严重
choices.pinyin: Yuè chī yào, wèntí kěnéng yuè yánzhòng.
choices.english: The more medicine she takes, the worse it may get.

questions.why: He backs 非去不可 with his sister's story: she put it off, the pain grew until she couldn't eat, and it cost far more. That happened to the sister, not to the woman; waiting cost the sister more, not less; and it is putting it off, not the medicine, that he says made things worse.

intro.speaker: N
intro.traditional: 請聽一段對話，然後回答三個問題。
intro.simplified: 请听一段对话，然后回答三个问题。
intro.pinyin: Qǐng tīng yí duàn duìhuà, ránhòu huídá sān ge wèntí.
intro.english: Listen to a conversation, then answer three questions.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 聽說你爸爸上個星期住院了？現在怎麼樣？
lines.simplified: 听说你爸爸上个星期住院了？现在怎么样？
lines.pinyin: Tīngshuō nǐ bàba shàng ge xīngqí zhùyuàn le? Xiànzài zěnmeyàng?
lines.english: I hear your dad was in hospital last week. How is he now?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 已經回家了。他肚子不舒服了好幾個月，我們一再叫他去看醫生，他都說沒什麼。
lines.simplified: 已经回家了。他肚子不舒服了好几个月，我们一再叫他去看医生，他都说没什么。
lines.pinyin: Yǐjīng huíjiā le. Tā dùzi bù shūfú le hǎojǐ ge yuè, wǒmen yízài jiào tā qù kàn yīshēng, tā dōu shuō méi shénme.
lines.english: He's home now. His stomach had been bad for months. We told him again and again to see a doctor, and he always said it was nothing.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 那後來怎麼會去？
lines.simplified: 那后来怎么会去？
lines.pinyin: Nà hòulái zěnme huì qù?
lines.english: So how did he end up going?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 直到上星期痛得站不起來，他才肯讓我們送他去醫院。
lines.simplified: 直到上星期痛得站不起来，他才肯让我们送他去医院。
lines.pinyin: Zhídào shàng xīngqí tòng de zhàn bù qǐlái, tā cái kěn ràng wǒmen sòng tā qù yīyuàn.
lines.english: Not until last week, when it hurt so much he couldn't stand up, did he let us take him to hospital.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 醫生怎麼說？
lines.simplified: 医生怎么说？
lines.pinyin: Yīshēng zěnme shuō?
lines.english: What did the doctor say?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 還好不算太嚴重。好好吃藥，一兩個月就會好，只不過以後一杯酒都不能喝了。
lines.simplified: 还好不算太严重。好好吃药，一两个月就会好，只不过以后一杯酒都不能喝了。
lines.pinyin: Háihǎo bú suàn tài yánzhòng. Hǎohǎo chī yào, yì liǎng ge yuè jiù huì hǎo, zhǐbúguò yǐhòu yì bēi jiǔ dōu bù néng hē le.
lines.english: Luckily it's not too serious. If he takes his medicine he'll be fine in a month or two; it's just that he can never drink a drop of alcohol again.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 他做生意，常常要跟客人喝酒吧？
lines.simplified: 他做生意，常常要跟客人喝酒吧？
lines.pinyin: Tā zuò shēngyì, chángcháng yào gēn kèrén hē jiǔ ba?
lines.english: He's in business. He has to drink with clients a lot, doesn't he?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 對啊。他說不能喝酒，以後怎麼跟客人談生意。
lines.simplified: 对啊。他说不能喝酒，以后怎么跟客人谈生意。
lines.pinyin: Duì a. Tā shuō bù néng hē jiǔ, yǐhòu zěnme gēn kèrén tán shēngyì.
lines.english: Yes. He says if he can't drink, how is he supposed to do business with clients?

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 身體比生意重要。你們全家要多跟他溝通。
lines.simplified: 身体比生意重要。你们全家要多跟他沟通。
lines.pinyin: Shēntǐ bǐ shēngyì zhòngyào. Nǐmen quánjiā yào duō gēn tā gōutōng.
lines.english: His health matters more than business. Your whole family needs to talk it through with him.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的爸爸後來為什麼去了醫院？
prompt.simplified: 男的爸爸后来为什么去了医院？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de bàba hòulái wèishénme qù le yīyuàn?
prompt.english: Why did the man's father finally go to hospital?

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 家人一再叫他去看醫生
choices.simplified: 家人一再叫他去看医生
choices.pinyin: Jiārén yízài jiào tā qù kàn yīshēng.
choices.english: His family kept urging him to see a doctor.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 肚子痛得沒辦法走路了
choices.simplified: 肚子痛得没办法走路了
choices.pinyin: Dùzi tòng de méi bànfǎ zǒulù le.
choices.english: His stomach hurt too much to walk.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Gōngsī yào tā zuò jiànkāng jiǎnchá.
choices.english: His company made him have a checkup.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Kèrén péi tā qù kàn yīshēng.
choices.english: A client took him to see a doctor.

questions.why: 直到上星期痛得站不起來，他才肯…: the pain, not the family, got him there. 一再叫他去 is what had failed for months (他都說沒什麼), and no company checkup or client is mentioned.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的爸爸為什麼擔心以後的工作？
prompt.simplified: 男的爸爸为什么担心以后的工作？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de bàba wèishénme dānxīn yǐhòu de gōngzuò?
prompt.english: Why is the man's father worried about his work from now on?

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 談生意常常得陪客人喝酒
choices.simplified: 谈生意常常得陪客人喝酒
choices.pinyin: Tán shēngyì chángcháng děi péi kèrén hē jiǔ.
choices.english: Doing business often means drinking with clients.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 還得在醫院住一兩個月
choices.simplified: 还得在医院住一两个月
choices.pinyin: Hái děi zài yīyuàn zhù yì liǎng ge yuè.
choices.english: He still has to stay in hospital a month or two.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 醫生要他少跟客人吃飯
choices.simplified: 医生要他少跟客人吃饭
choices.pinyin: Yīshēng yào tā shǎo gēn kèrén chīfàn.
choices.english: The doctor wants him to eat out with clients less.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 家人要他少做一點生意
choices.simplified: 家人要他少做一点生意
choices.pinyin: Jiārén yào tā shǎo zuò yìdiǎn shēngyì.
choices.english: His family wants him to do less business.

questions.why: After 只不過 the doctor adds the lasting rule, no alcohol ever again, and the father asks how he can do business without drinking with clients. He is already home (一兩個月 is how long the medicine takes), the doctor said nothing about meals, and the family is only asked to talk with him.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 女的最後說的話是什麼意思？
prompt.simplified: 女的最后说的话是什么意思？
prompt.pinyin: Nǚ de zuìhòu shuō de huà shì shénme yìsi?
prompt.english: What does the woman mean by what she says last?

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 好好跟客人談，讓爸爸少喝酒
choices.simplified: 好好跟客人谈，让爸爸少喝酒
choices.pinyin: Hǎohǎo gēn kèrén tán, ràng bàba shǎo hē jiǔ.
choices.english: Talk it over with the clients so Dad drinks less.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 讓爸爸換一個不用喝酒的工作
choices.simplified: 让爸爸换一个不用喝酒的工作
choices.pinyin: Ràng bàba huàn yí ge bú yòng hē jiǔ de gōngzuò.
choices.english: Get Dad to change to a job without drinking.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 好好跟醫生談，讓爸爸多注意健康
choices.simplified: 好好跟医生谈，让爸爸多注意健康
choices.pinyin: Hǎohǎo gēn yīshēng tán, ràng bàba duō zhùyì jiànkāng.
choices.english: Talk it over with the doctor so Dad pays more attention to his health.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 好好跟爸爸談，讓他多注意健康
choices.simplified: 好好跟爸爸谈，让他多注意健康
choices.pinyin: Hǎohǎo gēn bàba tán, ràng tā duō zhùyì jiànkāng.
choices.english: Talk it over with Dad properly so he pays more attention to his health.

questions.why: 身體比生意重要。你們全家要多跟他溝通: talk with him until he puts health before business. 跟他 is Dad himself, not the doctor or the clients (the clients are his worry), and putting health first does not mean giving up his business.

intro.speaker: N
intro.traditional: 請聽一段對話，然後回答三個問題。
intro.simplified: 请听一段对话，然后回答三个问题。
intro.pinyin: Qǐng tīng yí duàn duìhuà, ránhòu huídá sān ge wèntí.
intro.english: Listen to a conversation, then answer three questions.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 你怎麼戴起眼鏡來了？你眼睛不是很好嗎？
lines.simplified: 你怎么戴起眼镜来了？你眼睛不是很好吗？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme dài qǐ yǎnjìng lái le? Nǐ yǎnjīng bú shì hěn hǎo ma?
lines.english: Since when do you wear glasses? Aren't your eyes good?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 上個月開始，黑板上的字越來越看不清楚。我以為只是太累了，直到上星期去檢查，才知道眼睛真的變差了。
lines.simplified: 上个月开始，黑板上的字越来越看不清楚。我以为只是太累了，直到上星期去检查，才知道眼睛真的变差了。
lines.pinyin: Shàng ge yuè kāishǐ, hēibǎn shàng de zì yuè lái yuè kàn bù qīngchǔ. Wǒ yǐwéi zhǐ shì tài lèi le, zhídào shàng xīngqí qù jiǎnchá, cái zhīdào yǎnjīng zhēn de biàn chà le.
lines.english: From last month the writing on the board got harder and harder to read. I thought I was just tired; not until I had my eyes checked last week did I find out they had really got worse.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 是不是手機看太多了？
lines.simplified: 是不是手机看太多了？
lines.pinyin: Shì bú shì shǒujī kàn tài duō le?
lines.english: Is it from looking at your phone too much?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 醫生也這麼說。我每天躺在床上看影片，常常看到半夜兩三點。我媽一再說這樣對眼睛不好，我都沒聽。
lines.simplified: 医生也这么说。我每天躺在床上看影片，常常看到半夜两三点。我妈一再说这样对眼睛不好，我都没听。
lines.pinyin: Yīshēng yě zhème shuō. Wǒ měi tiān tǎng zài chuáng shàng kàn yǐngpiàn, chángcháng kàn dào bànyè liǎng sān diǎn. Wǒ mā yízài shuō zhèyàng duì yǎnjīng bù hǎo, wǒ dōu méi tīng.
lines.english: That's what the doctor said too. Every day I lie in bed watching videos, often until two or three in the morning. My mom told me again and again it was bad for my eyes, and I never listened.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 那你現在還看嗎？
lines.simplified: 那你现在还看吗？
lines.pinyin: Nà nǐ xiànzài hái kàn ma?
lines.english: So do you still watch?

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 醫生說要是不改，眼睛會越來越差。所以我現在十二點以前就把手機放到客廳去。
lines.simplified: 医生说要是不改，眼睛会越来越差。所以我现在十二点以前就把手机放到客厅去。
lines.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō yàoshì bù gǎi, yǎnjīng huì yuè lái yuè chà. Suǒyǐ wǒ xiànzài shí'èr diǎn yǐqián jiù bǎ shǒujī fàng dào kètīng qù.
lines.english: The doctor said if I don't change, my eyes will keep getting worse. So now I put my phone in the living room before twelve.

lines.speaker: F
lines.traditional: 你媽一定很高興吧？
lines.simplified: 你妈一定很高兴吧？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ mā yídìng hěn gāoxìng ba?
lines.english: Your mom must be pleased.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 她說她講了三年都沒用，醫生才說一次就有用了。
lines.simplified: 她说她讲了三年都没用，医生才说一次就有用了。
lines.pinyin: Tā shuō tā jiǎng le sān nián dōu méi yòng, yīshēng cái shuō yí cì jiù yǒu yòng le.
lines.english: She says she told me for three years and it did nothing, and the doctor said it just once and it worked.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的是什麼時候知道眼睛真的變差的？
prompt.simplified: 男的是什么时候知道眼睛真的变差的？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de shì shénme shíhòu zhīdào yǎnjīng zhēn de biàn chà de?
prompt.english: When did the man find out his eyes had really got worse?

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Shàng xīngqí zuò le jiǎnchá yǐhòu.
choices.english: After his eye check last week.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 上個月覺得很累的時候
choices.simplified: 上个月觉得很累的时候
choices.pinyin: Shàng ge yuè juéde hěn lèi de shíhòu.
choices.english: Last month, when he felt very tired.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 看影片看到半夜的時候
choices.simplified: 看影片看到半夜的时候
choices.pinyin: Kàn yǐngpiàn kàn dào bànyè de shíhòu.
choices.english: When he watched videos until late at night.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 開始看不清楚黑板的時候
choices.simplified: 开始看不清楚黑板的时候
choices.pinyin: Kāishǐ kàn bù qīngchǔ hēibǎn de shíhòu.
choices.english: When he first couldn't read the board.

questions.why: 我以為只是太累了，直到上星期去檢查，才知道…: when the board got blurry he blamed tiredness, and only the check last week showed the truth. The late-night videos are the cause, not the moment he learned it.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的為什麼把手機放到客廳去？
prompt.simplified: 男的为什么把手机放到客厅去？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de wèishénme bǎ shǒujī fàng dào kètīng qù?
prompt.english: Why does the man put his phone in the living room?

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 才不會在床上看到半夜
choices.simplified: 才不会在床上看到半夜
choices.pinyin: Cái bú huì zài chuáng shàng kàn dào bànyè.
choices.english: So that he won't watch in bed until late at night.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Nǚ de jiào tā shǎo kàn shǒujī.
choices.english: The woman told him to use his phone less.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 醫生叫他把手機放在客廳
choices.simplified: 医生叫他把手机放在客厅
choices.pinyin: Yīshēng jiào tā bǎ shǒujī fàng zài kètīng.
choices.english: The doctor told him to keep his phone in the living room.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 在客廳看影片眼睛比較不累
choices.simplified: 在客厅看影片眼睛比较不累
choices.pinyin: Zài kètīng kàn yǐngpiàn yǎnjīng bǐjiào bú lèi.
choices.english: Watching videos in the living room is easier on his eyes.

questions.why: He used to lie in bed watching videos until two or three; once the doctor warned 要是不改…, he moved the phone out of the bedroom so he can't do that. The woman only asked a question, the doctor said to change but not where to put the phone, and he puts the phone away rather than watching in another room.

prompt.speaker: N
prompt.traditional: 男的媽媽說的話是什麼意思？
prompt.simplified: 男的妈妈说的话是什么意思？
prompt.pinyin: Nán de māma shuō de huà shì shénme yìsi?
prompt.english: What does the man's mother mean?

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Tā hěn gǎnxiè nà wèi yīshēng.
choices.english: She is very grateful to the doctor.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 兒子三年前眼睛就不好了
choices.simplified: 儿子三年前眼睛就不好了
choices.pinyin: Érzi sān nián qián yǎnjīng jiù bù hǎo le.
choices.english: Her son's eyes went bad three years ago.

choices.speaker: N
choices.traditional: 她覺得醫生說得太嚴重
choices.simplified: 她觉得医生说得太严重
choices.pinyin: Tā juéde yīshēng shuō de tài yánzhòng.
choices.english: She thinks the doctor exaggerated.

choices.speaker: N
choices.pinyin: Érzi bǐjiào tīng yīshēng de huà.
choices.english: Her son listens to the doctor more than to her.

questions.why: She 一再 said it was bad for his eyes and he 都沒聽, so 她講了三年都沒用，醫生才說一次就有用了 is a half-joking complaint: he ignored her and obeyed the doctor at once. The three years are how long she nagged, not how long his eyes were bad, and she agrees with the doctor.

focus.en: again and again; what someone means

intro.speaker: N
intro.traditional: 請聽一段廣播，然後回答三個問題。
intro.simplified: 请听一段广播，然后回答三个问题。
intro.pinyin: Qǐng tīng yí duàn guǎngbò, ránhòu huídá sān ge wèntí.
intro.english: Listen to a broadcast, then answer three questions.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 社區的各位朋友大家好，這裡是社區服務中心。
lines.simplified: 社区的各位朋友大家好，这里是社区服务中心。
lines.pinyin: Shèqū de gèwèi péngyǒu dàjiā hǎo, zhèlǐ shì shèqū fúwù zhōngxīn.
lines.english: Hello, everyone in the community. This is the community service centre.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 上個星期我們說過，為了讓大家更了解自己的健康情況，社區這個月跟附近的醫院合作，舉辦基本健康檢查。
lines.simplified: 上个星期我们说过，为了让大家更了解自己的健康情况，社区这个月跟附近的医院合作，举办基本健康检查。
lines.pinyin: Shàng ge xīngqí wǒmen shuō guo, wèile ràng dàjiā gèng liǎojiě zìjǐ de jiànkāng qíngkuàng, shèqū zhège yuè gēn fùjìn de yīyuàn hézuò, jǔbàn jīběn jiànkāng jiǎnchá.
lines.english: Last week we told you that, to help everyone know more about their health, the community is working with a nearby hospital this month to hold basic health checkups.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 因為醫院那天醫生不夠，所以檢查從二十號星期六，改到二十一號星期天。
lines.simplified: 因为医院那天医生不够，所以检查从二十号星期六，改到二十一号星期天。
lines.pinyin: Yīnwèi yīyuàn nà tiān yīshēng bú gòu, suǒyǐ jiǎnchá cóng èrshí hào xīngqíliù, gǎi dào èrshíyī hào xīngqítiān.
lines.english: Because the hospital is short of doctors that day, the checkup is moving from Saturday the 20th to Sunday the 21st.

lines.speaker: M

passage.traditional: 我爸爸以前很少運動，下班就坐在沙發上看電視。醫生{1}提醒他要多運動，他每次都只說「好」，從來沒做到。直到今年他爬到三樓就累得要休息，才開始每天去公園跑步。剛開始，他跑十分鐘就想{2}，可是他說，{3}是自己決定的事，就要堅持到底。我媽也{4}讓他跑完就有飯吃，特地把晚餐時間改到八點。半年後，他的身體好了很多，{5}晚上睡得比以前好：以前常常睡不著，現在一躺下就睡著了。他常說，{6}他早幾年開始運動，身體就不會變得那麼差。
passage.simplified: 我爸爸以前很少运动，下班就坐在沙发上看电视。医生{1}提醒他要多运动，他每次都只说「好」，从来没做到。直到今年他爬到三楼就累得要休息，才开始每天去公园跑步。刚开始，他跑十分钟就想{2}，可是他说，{3}是自己决定的事，就要坚持到底。我妈也{4}让他跑完就有饭吃，特地把晚餐时间改到八点。半年后，他的身体好了很多，{5}晚上睡得比以前好：以前常常睡不着，现在一躺下就睡着了。他常说，{6}他早几年开始运动，身体就不会变得那么差。
passage.pinyin: Wǒ bàba yǐqián hěn shǎo yùndòng, xiàbān jiù zuò zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì. Yīshēng yízài tíxǐng tā yào duō yùndòng, tā měi cì dōu zhǐ shuō "hǎo", cónglái méi zuò dào. Zhídào jīnnián tā pá dào sān lóu jiù lèi de yào xiūxí, cái kāishǐ měi tiān qù gōngyuán pǎobù. Gāng kāishǐ, tā pǎo shí fēnzhōng jiù xiǎng tíng xiàlái xiūxí, kěshì tā shuō, jìrán shì zìjǐ juédìng de shì, jiù yào jiānchí dàodǐ. Wǒ mā yě wèile ràng tā pǎo wán jiù yǒu fàn chī, tèdì bǎ wǎncān shíjiān gǎi dào bā diǎn. Bàn nián hòu, tā de shēntǐ hǎo le hěn duō, yóuqí wǎnshàng shuì de bǐ yǐqián hǎo: yǐqián chángcháng shuì bù zháo, xiànzài yì tǎng xià jiù shuìzháo le. Tā cháng shuō, jiǎrú tā zǎo jǐ nián kāishǐ yùndòng, shēntǐ jiù bú huì biàn de nàme chà.
passage.english: My dad used to hardly exercise; after work he would just sit on the sofa watching TV. The doctor reminded him again and again to exercise more, and every time he just said "OK" and never did it. Not until this year, when climbing to the third floor left him needing a rest, did he start running in the park every day. At first he wanted to stop for a rest after ten minutes, but he said that since it was his own decision, he had to stick with it to the end. So that he would have dinner ready as soon as he finished running, my mom made a point of moving dinner to eight. Six months on, his health is much better, especially his sleep at night: he used to have trouble sleeping, and now he falls asleep as soon as he lies down. He often says that if he had started exercising a few years earlier, his health would never have got so bad.

Suǒyǐ tā gēn lǎobǎn hǎohǎo gōutōng le yí cì, xiànzài měi tiān liù diǎn jiù xiàbān, wǎnshàng hái huì qù gōngyuán zǒuzou. passage.english: My older sister works at a computer company. She is often so busy she doesn't eat dinner until ten at night, and she works at home at weekends too. She would like to leave work earlier too; it's just that her boss keeps giving her new work, and she really can't get away. Last month, walking to the MRT station after work, her head suddenly felt heavy, she felt ill all over, and she couldn't even walk. She thought she just hadn't slept well, but to her surprise the doctor said it was all caused by overwork and told her to adjust her daily schedule at once. So she had a proper talk with her boss, and now she leaves at six every day and goes for a walk in the park in the evening. She says that she used to ignore her health to get her work done, and now she knows that however important work is, it is not as important as health.

text.traditional: 我媽媽在市場賣菜，一天要站十幾個小時。去年她的腳常常痛，醫生說她得多運動，最好去游泳，因為游泳對腳的負擔比較小。可是媽媽小時候在河邊玩水，差一點出了意外，從那時候起就很怕水。我一再叫她去學，她都說：「我都五十幾歲了，還學什麼游泳？」後來，我發現社區的游泳池有一個給年紀比較大的人上的班，就陪她去看了一次。她看到班上有幾位七十幾歲的老太太游得很開心，才答應試試看。剛開始，她連把頭放進水裡都不敢，上了三次課就不想學了。老師對她說：「既然來了，就學到底吧！我也一定會一直教到妳會。」媽媽為了不讓老師白教，每個星期都去上兩次課，一次也沒請過假。半年以後，她已經能游五十公尺了，腳也不那麼痛了。現在她每天早上都去游泳，還交了好幾個新朋友。她常說，學游泳不難，最難的是第一次走進游泳池。

Kěshì māma xiǎo shíhòu zài hébiān wán shuǐ, chàyìdiǎn chū le yìwài, cóng nà shíhòu qǐ jiù hěn pà shuǐ. Wǒ yízài jiào tā qù xué, tā dōu shuō: "Wǒ dōu wǔshí jǐ suì le, hái xué shénme yóuyǒng?" Hòulái, wǒ fāxiàn shèqū de yóuyǒngchí yǒu yí ge gěi niánjì bǐjiào dà de rén shàng de bān, jiù péi tā qù kàn le yí cì. Tā kàndào bān shàng yǒu jǐ wèi qīshí jǐ suì de lǎo tàitai yóu de hěn kāixīn, cái dāyìng shìshi kàn. Gāng kāishǐ, tā lián bǎ tóu fàng jìn shuǐ lǐ dōu bù gǎn, shàng le sān cì kè jiù bù xiǎng xué le. Lǎoshī duì tā shuō: "Jìrán lái le, jiù xué dàodǐ ba! Wǒ yě yídìng huì yìzhí jiāo dào nǐ huì." Māma wèile bú ràng lǎoshī bái jiāo, měi ge xīngqí dōu qù shàng liǎng cì kè, yí cì yě méi qǐng guo jià. Bàn nián yǐhòu, tā yǐjīng néng yóu wǔshí gōngchǐ le, jiǎo yě bú nàme tòng le. Xiànzài tā měi tiān zǎoshàng dōu qù yóuyǒng, hái jiāo le hǎojǐ ge xīn péngyǒu. Tā cháng shuō, xué yóuyǒng bù nán, zuì nán de shì dì yī cì zǒu jìn yóuyǒngchí.
text.english: My mother sells vegetables at the market and stands for over ten hours a day. Last year her feet often hurt. The doctor said she needed more exercise, ideally swimming, because swimming puts less strain on the feet. But when she was little she nearly had an accident playing in a river, and she has been afraid of water ever since. I told her to learn again and again, and she always said, "I'm already in my fifties. Why would I learn to swim now?" Later I found that the community pool had a class for older people, and I took her to have a look. When she saw several women in their seventies in the class swimming happily, she agreed to give it a try. At first she didn't even dare put her head under the water, and after three lessons she wanted to stop. The teacher told her, "Since you've come, see it through! And I'll keep teaching you until you can do it." So that the teacher's work wouldn't be wasted, she went to two lessons every week and never once took a day off. Six months later she could swim fifty metres, and her feet didn't hurt so much. Now she swims every morning and has made several new friends. She often says learning to swim isn't hard; the hardest part is walking into the pool the first time.

text.traditional: 我一個人在臺北工作，因為很忙，三餐都在外面吃，不是小吃就是泡麵。去年公司做健康檢查，報告上好幾個數字都不太好。醫生一再提醒我，外面的東西又油又鹹，假如不改變飲食習慣，以後毛病會越來越多。我這才決定自己煮飯。剛開始我什麼都不會，第一次煮的湯淡得沒有味道，第二次又鹹得沒辦法喝，我差一點就不想做了。我媽知道以後，每個星期天晚上都打電話來，很有耐心地教我做一道菜。她說：「學做菜跟做別的事一樣，要學就學到底。」三個月以後，我已經會做十幾道菜了。今年再去健檢，那些數字都好多了。現在我每天帶自己做的午餐上班，同事都說我的菜看起來比餐廳的還好吃，還常常問我是怎麼做的。對我來說，自己煮飯的好處不只是身體變好了，還讓我跟媽媽多了很多可以聊的話題。
text.simplified: 我一个人在台北工作，因为很忙，三餐都在外面吃，不是小吃就是泡面。去年公司做健康检查，报告上好几个数字都不太好。医生一再提醒我，外面的东西又油又咸，假如不改变饮食习惯，以后毛病会越来越多。我这才决定自己煮饭。刚开始我什么都不会，第一次煮的汤淡得没有味道，第二次又咸得没办法喝，我差一点就不想做了。我妈知道以后，每个星期天晚上都打电话来，很有耐心地教我做一道菜。她说：「学做菜跟做别的事一样，要学就学到底。」三个月以后，我已经会做十几道菜了。今年再去健检，那些数字都好多了。现在我每天带自己做的午餐上班，同事都说我的菜看起来比餐厅的还好吃，还常常问我是怎么做的。对我来说，自己煮饭的好处不只是身体变好了，还让我跟妈妈多了很多可以聊的话题。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yí ge rén zài Táiběi gōngzuò, yīnwèi hěn máng, sān cān dōu zài wàimiàn chī, bú shì xiǎochī jiù shì pàomiàn. Qùnián gōngsī zuò jiànkāng jiǎnchá, bàogào shàng hǎojǐ ge shùzì dōu bú tài hǎo. Yīshēng yízài tíxǐng wǒ, wàimiàn de dōngxi yòu yóu yòu xián, jiǎrú bù gǎibiàn yǐnshí xíguàn, yǐhòu máobìng huì yuè lái yuè duō. Wǒ zhè cái juédìng zìjǐ zhǔ fàn. Gāng kāishǐ wǒ shénme dōu bú huì, dì yī cì zhǔ de tāng dàn de méiyǒu wèidào, dì èr cì yòu xián de méi bànfǎ hē, wǒ chàyìdiǎn jiù bù xiǎng zuò le. Wǒ mā zhīdào yǐhòu, měi ge xīngqítiān wǎnshàng dōu dǎ diànhuà lái, hěn yǒu nàixīn de jiāo wǒ zuò yí dào cài. Tā shuō: "Xué zuò cài gēn zuò bié de shì yíyàng, yào xué jiù xué dàodǐ." Sān ge yuè yǐhòu, wǒ yǐjīng huì zuò shí jǐ dào cài le. Jīnnián zài qù jiànjiǎn, nàxiē shùzì dōu hǎo duō le. Xiànzài wǒ měi tiān dài zìjǐ zuò de wǔcān shàngbān, tóngshì dōu shuō wǒ de cài kàn qǐlái bǐ cāntīng de hái hǎochī, hái chángcháng wèn wǒ shì zěnme zuò de. Duì wǒ lái shuō, zìjǐ zhǔ fàn de hǎochù bù zhǐ shì shēntǐ biàn hǎo le, hái ràng wǒ gēn māma duō le hěn duō kěyǐ liáo de huàtí.
text.english: I work in Taipei on my own. Because I'm busy, I eat all three meals out: if it's not street snacks, it's instant noodles. Last year my company held health checkups, and several numbers on my report weren't good. The doctor reminded me again and again that food outside is oily and salty, and that if I didn't change my eating habits I would have more and more health problems. Only then did I decide to cook for myself. At first I couldn't do anything: the first soup I made was so bland it had no taste, the second so salty I couldn't drink it, and I nearly gave up. When my mom found out, she started phoning every Sunday evening to teach me one dish, very patiently. She said, "Learning to cook is like anything else: if you're going to learn, learn it properly to the end." Three months later I could cook over a dozen dishes. At this year's checkup those numbers were much better. Now I bring a lunch I made myself to work every day, and my colleagues say my food looks better than a restaurant's and often ask how I make it. For me, cooking for myself hasn't just made me healthier; it has also given me and my mom lots more to talk about.
